public_rationale: The checkable part is a hedged conditional: if the debt spigot is turned off, things will not be pretty. The antecedent has not happened. Tech borrowing reached about $500B in the first nine months of 2026, and reporting said the AI financing boom was not stalling. Debt got more expensive, and by October there were worries about a financing crunch, but lenders kept lending. Because the condition did not occur, the forecast cannot be scored. The first sentence, that basically everything in tech depends on debt, is too broad and has no measure to test.
limitations: The antecedent could still occur after the evaluation date, given tightening credit in October 2026.
The claim is hedged as a personal belief.

The growth of private credit is so recent that we truly don’t know what happens if the debt spigot gets turned off, but I do not think it will be pretty.

our_interpretation: The checkable part is conditional: if the debt spigot is turned off, the result will be bad for tech finance.
Antecedent: debt for tech and AI largely stops being available, meaning lenders broadly refuse to lend, not just charge more.
The first sentence ('depends on the near-perpetual availability of debt') is a broad, rhetorical statement with no measure. He also hedges ('we truly don't know', 'I do not think').
criteria.support_condition: The debt spigot is turned off, and widespread financing failures or distress follow in PE, private credit, VC and tech.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The debt spigot is turned off, and tech financing carries on without serious distress.
